newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares rise but foreigners eye crown.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares rise but foreigners eye crown.

text.p: Czech major issues rebounded on Thursday but dealers said buying was almost exclusivley domestic while foreigners waited nervously for a resolution of the current crisis surrounding the crown.
The Reuters RPIX index of continuously traded shares closed up 13.7 points, 1.43 percent to 970.7 with Komercni Banka rising 82 crowns to 1,714 and SPT Telecom gaining 60 crowns to 2,910.
Dealers said trading had been intense throughout the session but was mainly domestically driven with investors taking advantage of cheap buying opportunities after several weeks of sharp falls.
Foreign investors were seen staying on the sidelines pending the outcome of the current battle between foreign currency speculators and the Czech National Bank (CNB) over the fate of the crown.
"Foreign clients are waiting to see if there will be a devaluation of the crown," said Ivan kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.
"I havent seen foreign buyers today....I don't think foreign buyers will trade until the situation of the crown is stabilised," added ING Baring's Lubomir Vystavel.
The crown has been under attack since early morning and the CNB has taken a variety of measures ranging from direct inervention to closing off access to the last resort Lombard rate, to prop it up.
Just after the end of continuous trading the crown was trading at around 4.0 percent below the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket from 2.5 percent at the open.
Vystavel said activity was heavy and volatile.
"It's quite hectic, there is a lot of trading, prices go up and suddenly down," he said.
